chapter: Ellington, singers, the book and closing
title: Pocket-sized bombs, Red Brigades and the Mafia
summary: Idle talk about who knows where the button is, Japanese protesters and the Mafia.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Politics, race and the state of the country

blocks.x: You know something, man? Some cat is going to get very bugged, and push that button.
There are more people, I'm beginning to find out, who know where that button is. It's not only the President.
Yeah, I know.

There are other people in the Strategic Command, and you get some of these people like the Red Brigades in Italy, that kidnapped the Prime Minister, if they ever get access to that information, forget it. I mean, they got that atomic bomb thing down so you could put it in something this size, carry it in your pocket.
Yeah, pocket. The Japanese did that.
(Inaudible.)
I wrote that in my book, man, the Japanese are going to make a pocket-sized one.
I'm sure they will, I'm sure they will. They are the most terrifying of all the protesters. Did you see what they did to that airport, when the new airport opened up?
(Inaudible.)
The Japanese. The kids didn't want the airport to open up. I'm not sure why, I guess --
They built something.
They took over the control tower, and tore it apart. They had 14,000 cops. I don't know why they couldn't stop it. Apparently it'll be eight or ten months before they can --
(Inaudible.)
(Inaudible.)

Oh, really? Because I saw in the Washington Post today that the Mafia in Italy, the home team, have threatened the Brigades, the radicals, that if they don't turn him back they will assassinate those of the Red Brigade who are on trial now in Truro, which is playing heavy stakes.
Yeah, because nobody -- the Mafia will do it, too, because they're underground.
Oh, yeah, they have to (inaudible) if they make the --
They're old as Christ. The Mafia is as old as Christ, you know.
But if they make the threat, they got to do it.
The Mafia protected Christianity for the Catholic Church.
(End of proceedings as recorded.)
